title: Go compiler parser (cmd/compile/internal/syntax/parser.go)
why: The Go compiler's own recursive-descent parser, showing precedence-driven binary expression parsing.

title: Go compiler parser tokens (cmd/compile/internal/syntax/tokens.go)
why: Defines the Operator enum with one precedence constant per level, the source of the precedence each operator token carries.

title: GCC 3.4 Release Series: Changes, New Features, and Fixes
why: States that GCC 3.4 replaced the YACC-derived C++ parser with a hand-written recursive-descent parser.

title: GCC 4.1 Release Series: Changes, New Features, and Fixes
why: States that GCC 4.1 replaced the Bison-based C parser with a hand-written recursive-descent parser.

title: clang/lib/Parse/ParseExpr.cpp
why: Clang's expression parser, whose comments call it a precedence-based parser and whose ParseRHSOfBinaryExpression takes a minimum precedence.

title: Overview of the compiler (Rust Compiler Development Guide)
why: States that rustc's parser uses a recursive descent (top-down) approach and names its entry points in rustc_parse.

title: Go runtime stack growth (src/runtime/stack.go)
why: The exact runtime code that prints the goroutine stack-exceeds message and throws the stack overflow fatal error.

title: Package runtime/debug
why: Official documentation for SetMaxStack, including the default 1 GB limit on 64-bit systems.

claim: The Go compiler parses binary expressions with a recursive binaryExpr function that takes a precedence argument and keeps absorbing operators while the current token's precedence is greater than that argument.
Each operator token produced by the Go compiler's scanner carries its own precedence value in a prec field.
quote:
op        Operator // valid if tok is _Operator, _Star, _AssignOp, or _IncOp
	prec      int      // valid if tok is _Operator, _Star, _AssignOp, or _IncOp

locator: C++ section of the release notes
claim: GCC 3.4 replaced the YACC-derived C++ parser with a hand-written recursive-descent C++ parser.
quote: - A hand-written recursive-descent C++ parser has replaced the YACC-derived C++ parser from previous GCC releases.

locator: C and Objective-C section of the release notes
claim: GCC 4.1 replaced the old Bison-based C and Objective-C parser with a new, faster hand-written recursive-descent parser.
quote: - The old Bison-based C and Objective-C parser has been replaced by a new, faster hand-written recursive-descent parser.

claim: Clang's Parser library is a recursive-descent parser that polls tokens from the preprocessor.
quote: This library contains a recursive-descent parser that polls tokens from the preprocessor and notifies a client of the parsing progress.

claim: Clang's expression parser is described in its own source comment as a simple precedence-based parser for binary and ternary operators.
quote: /// Simple precedence-based parser for binary/ternary operators.

claim: rustc's parser turns the token stream into an AST using a recursive descent (top-down) approach to syntax analysis.
quote: The parser translates the token stream from the lexer into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It uses a recursive descent (top-down) approach to syntax analysis.

claim: rustc's parser implementation lives in rustc_parse, specifically rustc_parse::parser.
quote: The parser is defined in rustc_parse, along with a high-level interface to the lexer and some validation routines that run after macro expansion. In particular, the rustc_parse::parser contains the parser implementation.

claim: SetMaxStack's initial setting is 1 GB on 64-bit systems and 250 MB on 32-bit systems, and the program crashes if a goroutine exceeds the limit while growing its stack.
quote: SetMaxStack sets the maximum amount of memory that can be used by a single goroutine stack. If any goroutine exceeds this limit while growing its stack, the program crashes. SetMaxStack returns the previous setting. The initial setting is 1 GB on 64-bit systems, 250 MB on 32-bit systems.

claim: When growing a goroutine's stack would exceed the limit, the runtime prints "runtime: goroutine stack exceeds <limit>-byte limit" and then throws "stack overflow".
